p:cNvPr.descr: Part 1: A three-part diagram, labeled a, b, and c, that illustrates the lac operon. Part a shows a long, narrow rectangular structure divided into 13 segments, each separated by a short black line. Starting from the left to the right, the structure is labeled 5’, followed by a short blue segment, a short purple segment labeled P (subscript I), a pink segment labeled lacI, and an orange segment labeled O (subscript 3). In between P (subscript I) and lacI is an arrow that points up and to the right. To the right of O (subscript 3) is another short blue segment, followed by a purple P labeled P, an orange segment labeled O (subscript I), and a tan segment labeled lacZ. In between O (subscript I) and lacZ is an arrow that points up and to the right. To the right of lacZ is another orange segment labeled O (subscript 2), a short tan segment, a peach-colored segment labeled lacY, a yellow segment of the same size, labeled lacA, and a short blue segment; this entire chain ends with a 3’ on the right. The two short lines that border O (subscript 1) to the left and right point to a rectangular box that has two rows of letter sequences. The first row starts with 5’ and shows AATTGT, shaded tan, followed by GAGCGGATA (not shaded), followed by ACAATT, shaded orange, and ends with 3’. The second row starts with 3’, followed by TTAACA, shaded orange, CTCGCCTAT (not shaded), followed by TGTTAA, shaded tan, followed by a 5’. In part b, the rectangular structure described in part a is shown, except it is slightly folded and looped between O (subscript 3) and O (subscript 1), so the blue segment and purple segment labeled P are crossed and shown as the loop above the rectangle. Below the looped section is a pink structure with four oddly-shaped tentacles attached to O (subscript 3) and O (subscript 1). Below this is part c, which shows the same structure described in part a, but this time the loops occur between O (subscript 1) and O (subscript 2), so that the loop is created by lacZ. The same pink, tentacle structure has now moved down the rectangle to where O (subscript 1) and O (subscript 2) are located. Two lines point from this area to a square that has two globular masses that are connected at the bottom middle, and which appear to be mirror-images of each other. The structure on the left has a burgundy outer edge, a pink middle, and a burgundy top right piece. On top of the entire structure are three arched lines that have yellow extensions underneath them; the extensions connect to the top surface of the globular mass. The globular mass to the right is similar; however, it has a red, left outer section that extends to the top right, and a burgundy middle section that begins at the top left and travels down the rest of the structure. It too has the lined arches with yellow extensions at the top of its surface.
